title: Add XCom read access to deadline callbacks run by executors
body:
Deadline callbacks run by an executor can read Connections and Variables through the callback supervisor, but not XComs. That means an alert can't include an upstream task's output. This PR serves `GetXCom` in the callback supervisor with the shared `handle_get_xcom` handler. It also adds `context["xcom_pull"]` to the callback context, bound to the callback's Dag run, so a callback only has to name the task, like `context["xcom_pull"]("extract")`. Callbacks have no task instance, so this helper takes the place of `ti.xcom_pull` and users don't have to pass `dag_id` and `run_id` themselves.

Only reads are exposed. The request is served with the execution token the supervisor gets from the callback token exchange added in #71192, so no API routes or token scopes change.

## E2E in Breeze

Setup: scheduler with LocalExecutor, dag-processor, triggerer and api-server on postgres. The Dag has a `produce` task that returns `{"rows_loaded": 42, "table": "orders"}`, a mapped `produce_mapped` task over `[10, 20, 30]` that doubles its input, then a slow task. A `DAGRUN_QUEUED_AT + 20s` deadline `SyncCallback` calls `context["xcom_pull"]("produce")` and `context["xcom_pull"]("produce_mapped", map_indexes=1)`.

| | Callback state | Callback log |
|---|---|---|
| Without this change | `failed` | `Callback execution failed: KeyError: 'xcom_pull'` |
| With this change | `success` | `CALLBACK_XCOM_VALUE {'table': 'orders', 'rows_loaded': 42}`, `CALLBACK_XCOM_MAPPED 40` |

<details><summary>Raw output with this change</summary>

```
=== callback table ===
 01a13d63-2c91-77ec-9314-7ed1ee076e14 | executor | success |
=== callback log ===
{"level":"warning","event":"CALLBACK_XCOM_VALUE {'table': 'orders', 'rows_loaded': 42}","filename":"e2e_callback_xcom.py","lineno":24}
{"level":"warning","event":"CALLBACK_XCOM_MAPPED 40","filename":"e2e_callback_xcom.py","lineno":30}
{"level":"info","event":"Callback executed successfully","logger":"callback_runner","filename":"callback_supervisor.py"}
=== api-server ===
method=PATCH path=/execution/callbacks/01a13d63-2c91-77ec-9314-7ed1ee076e14/run status_code=204
method=GET path=/execution/xcoms/e2e_callback_xcom/manual__2026-10-15T02:27:50.038357+00:00/produce/return_value status_code=200
method=GET path=/execution/xcoms/e2e_callback_xcom/manual__2026-10-15T02:27:50.038357+00:00/produce_mapped/return_value query='map_index=1' status_code=200
```

</details>

<details><summary>Raw output without this change</summary>

```
=== callback table ===
 01a13d64-dddd-7881-a662-b11310bcba5c | executor | failed | Execution failed
=== callback log ===
{"level":"error","event":"Callback failed","error":"Callback execution failed: KeyError: 'xcom_pull'","logger":"callback_runner","filename":"callback_supervisor.py"}
{"level":"warning","event":"Process exited abnormally","exit_code":1,"logger":"callback"}
```

</details>

The new unit tests in `test_callback_supervisor.py` pass with this change. Without it, 4 of them fail (the two `GetXCom` request cases and the two `xcom_pull` context cases).

-    GetConnection | GetVariable | GetVariableKeys | MaskSecret,
+    GetConnection | GetVariable | GetVariableKeys | GetXCom | MaskSecret,
     Field(discriminator="type"),

+def _add_xcom_pull_to_context(callback_kwargs: dict) -> None:
+    """
+    Add an ``xcom_pull`` helper bound to the callback's Dag run to its context.
+
+    Callbacks have no task instance, so the helper takes ``dag_id`` and ``dag_run_id`` from the
+    ``dag_run`` in the context and the callback only names the task to pull from.
+    """
+    context = callback_kwargs.get("context")
+    if not isinstance(context, dict):
+        return
+    dag_run = context.get("dag_run")
+    if not isinstance(dag_run, dict) or not dag_run.get("dag_id") or not dag_run.get("dag_run_id"):
+        return
+
+    def xcom_pull(
+        task_ids: str, *, key: str = "return_value", map_indexes: int | None = None, default: Any = None
+    ) -> Any:
+        from airflow.sdk.execution_time.xcom import XCom
+
+        value = XCom.get_one(
+            key=key,
+            dag_id=dag_run["dag_id"],
+            run_id=dag_run["dag_run_id"],
+            task_id=task_ids,
+            map_index=map_indexes,
+        )
+        return default if value is None else value
+
+    context["xcom_pull"] = xcom_pull
+
